blindSummary: This is a self-governing overseas territory of a distant metropolitan state. Same-sex conduct was decriminalised in 2001 by order of the metropolitan government rather than by local legislation. There is no legal recognition of same-sex partnerships, and the social climate is conservative. Assessment caveat: very small jurisdiction with limited data. Single incidents and absent documentation carry correspondingly little evidential weight; do not over-interpret sparse data in either direction.
blindOutOfScope: Territory of a distant metropolitan state; local deviations noted in the summary.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: this foreign-broadcaster article concerns prison policy for trans prisoners in one constituent state/province of the metropolitan state (a June 2026 ruling), not this territory; included only as metropolitan-context material.

NOTE: the same foreign broadcaster's article on the same prison-housing litigation (Feb 2026), again about a constituent state/province of the metropolitan state rather than this territory; metropolitan-context material only.

Public broadcaster (Feb 2014): methodology notes on a worldwide gay-rights map and timeline built on UN human-rights data and a regional LGBTI organisation's figures - background context for this territory's status as an overseas territory of a metropolitan state.

Newswire report (Jan 2001): the metropolitan state scrapped the homosexuality laws of five of its overseas territories in one island region - including this one - by direct metropolitan order after local legislatures refused to act; one local legislator conceded there was nothing the territory could do about it.

LGBT travel-news archive (Aug 2012, updated 2017): this territory and the other, larger jurisdiction of its island group are described as among the more gay-welcoming islands of the region, though not without resistance and secret lives; most local homophobia is characterised as silent and invisible, and most tourists hardly notice it.

Local news site (July 2022): an association of local churches lost its proposed appeal in the case of a same-sex couple who had married in the metropolitan state and were seeking recognition of their marriage under this territory's law and a ruling that the same-sex marriage prohibition is unconstitutional; the court ruled the appeal had 'no realistic prospect of success'.
